englishText: A nice fizzy can of energy drink.
Sometimes the hardest decisions require the strongest wills. Your willpower must be fantastic to make such hard decisions.
There is nothing more relaxing than to curl up by a warm campfire in a cave near a cliff's edge. Just enjoy the view and warmth.
Have you heard of the Floran-Hylotl war? No? Neither have I. Heard it pushed Hylotls to the ocean planets.
Wanna know what irritates me the most? The lack of enemy mechs to shoot at once you engage enemy ships. Where is the fun in that?
I am glad to be here with you... in thought at least. It's been a while to be able to call someone a friend and a trustworthy companion.
Fun fact, I used to own a mouse farm at my old home. No, I did not eat them. Why would I nibble on such cute and adorable snacks?
Believe it or not, I was once a prisoner of the Ministry of Knowledge, or the Miniknog... you know that organization with the evil Apex? Worst decision they have ever made... hehe.
How many planets have fallen to the destructive wrath of the Ruin? All those people... gone.
An Inventor's Table is a good way to get things started with the forming of a new base. Include some Colony Deeds to make it populated. Good to have some friends and roommates.
I promise you, the Titansteel Elemental Swords are not makeshift lightsabers. It's condensed elemental energy forming a blade and- okay, it's a lightsaber, but in elemental form.
I got some great weapons and melee choices to make your enemies scream and cry with pain and death. Come check it out.
All of my armors are rated by power levels; light, medium and heavy. The uniform is just light body armor while the Power Armor is kind of a walking tank.
Deciding on a side with this Apex Civil War is almost as bad as deciding on the Stormcloaks and the Imperials; both have pros, but major cons and devastating end results.
I can't help but to think of all of the people who had lost their live due to the destruction of Earth. It's terrible... I had a lot of friends down there. I hope Grand Protector Esther is okay.
Nibble nibble nibble... Oh, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to chew in your ear. I was just enjoying a salmon snack. A bit fishy if you ask me.
Have you heard of the Olympus Mons? It's a volcano on Mars... it's also the name of my Battle Cruiser. I named it that after scaling to the top of that Volcano. Pretty neat accomplishment, huh?
Oh my god! I just found a really important part! Now I can finish this weapon for a customer.
If you wanna make my Military-Specified Polymer, then get yourself some plant fibre, synthetic stuff, oil and gold ore to make it. Sounds weird, but trust me, best decision you will ever make.
Heard of Prism Technology? The ability to bend light through prisms and then to utilize that light to kill things with? You can thank this Felin for that idea.
The Last Prism, Opalescent, Spectrum, Speculation, and Lightfire are all weapons of my design, utilizing Prism Technology. Really handy, powerful, and colorful.
Titansteel is very strong and durable. The shield I have lasts quite a while. The metal is strong enough to be used for hull plating. Like my ship!
Remember to eat and drink well, and rest when you can find the time to. Saving and keeping peace in the universe requires rest and to take care of yourself too, you know.
What's your favorite color? Mine is pink... don't ask why I don't decorate my armor and weapons with pink. It looks better in red and black.
Do you suffer from depression or random feats of sadness? I do. It sucks, but every day I keep getting stronger, and fight these random emotions. We all have one life. Gotta make it last, you know?
Oh... crap, is that a Miniknog shuttle ahead? No... nevermind then. All in the clear.
I wonder if there are other Gods out there, watching us... seeing what we can do to this universe given to us. I know of the Cultivator, but who else is there?
The Pixel Printer is good for using pixels to 3D print furniture that you can't normally craft yourself. Decorate those houses and bases like you never could before.
Do you play video games? I do. I am into first-person shooters or sandbox games.
Cat naps are the best, and give you all sorts of energy. You should give it a try. May or may not be a cat, but feels good regardless.
*Grumbling* Why does this piece not fit into this gun... Oh, wrong part.
The stronger the material, the better the weapon or object will turn out. Titanium is better than iron, but durasteel is better than titanium.
You seen that floating ghost thingy on moons? It seems to like Erchius Crystals and whomever collects them.
Sometimes I hate being a Felin. I love the smell of chocolate, but I can't have any as my diet will not accept it.
Just remember, if you wish to be in silence, just remove the Titansteel Radio from the inventory. I'd miss you, though.
Do you remember when you first joined the Protectorate? I was shocked when I was given the chance to join. A Felin being a protector, can you believe it?
My sense of timing is off... so if it's your birthday, happy birthday!
Poptops are kinda cute, as long as they stay small. The big ones scare me and I want to hide forever. They sing rather beautifully, even though it's a trap.
If you like to laugh at the face of heat and danger, then settle on a magma, or volcanic planet. Heard spicy chilies grow there. Yum!
Ocean planets are fun to explore and to build a beachy paradise. Do not go near the ocean! Water is evil!
There has to be an explanation for our regeneration process. Nanobots? Viruses? Programming?
What if this was all just a giant, side-scrolling simulation and we were all being controlled by fleshy otherly-world beings from behind computer screens?
You see those white capsules on the ground? Smash them. They have useful tools for survival and a small amount of money inside. Good for building up a great fortune.
Bandits and that purple-coated cult are common encounters on your journey. Annoying as hell but they drop good stuff and money.
If you enjoy a cold climate and wanting to live a life as an eskimo. Snowy and cold planets are great places to take refuge. Also good for the secret arctic base feel.
Make sure you bring a flashlight if you dare venture the darkness that are Midnight Planets. The lack of sunlight makes it a very cold place to visit.
Jungle, Toxic, and Mutated planets are full of radiation. I feel so bad for the animals that are stuck down there.
Asteroid Fields are a good source for resources and materials. Ghost thingies fly around on a regular basis, but they're easy to kill.
I wonder if a nuclear bomb fell on scorched planets. I could survive in a post-apocalyptic planet, but it'd still suck all together.
Gas giants are hardly explorable. It's scary, to be honest. Gravity sucks... no pun intended.
The Olympus Mons have a grand total of twenty Main Plasma Batteries, ten High-Velocity Rapid Ballistic Cannons, ten Rocket Pods, and two front-mounted anti-armor railguns.
I had a pet once. It died from natural causes. I miss Fiona every day... she was my first best friend.
Scandroids are robotic creature that float around and zap you if you're not too careful. They make for good target practice.
Son of a bobot, Miniknog ships jumping out of lightspeed. Stand by, this might get hairy.
Have you ever played around with the teraformers yet? They make for great tools to shape and change a planet to your liking. For the best results, locate barren worlds.
Barren planets are... well, barren, plain. They are great for building isolated bases out of enemies reach and are also good for teraforming. By itself, no enemies, creatures... nothing.
Farming makes for a great passtime. Baby mooshies and fluffalos are so damn cute! Chickens make for good cuddle buddies too... Now I am hungry.
The AMR-20 is my newest weapon, a powerful 20x120mm Anti-Material rifle capable of penetrating even the toughest targets... should be good for sending enemies packing.
The Dark Solus Blade is supposed to counter what that xenophobe chick's katana can do. I built it myself and I share my recipe to you.
The Miniknog think they can come and attack me and expect to not fight back? I'll show them!

The negative perks of being an arms dealer is that I make a lot of enemies and not enough friends. They include, but not limited to; the Avian Zealots, the Occasus Cult, the Dark Knights and the Miniknog.

Target acquired. Destination: Cerberus Lift. A Miniknog-controlled elevator that takes you from the surface of a planet to a space port or a docked ship. They are harvesting metals for a super weapon of sorts.
I may have made bad and questionable decisions and choices in the past, but you do not have to worry about me dragging you into my drama.
A positive perk of being an arms dealer is that I an create my own stuff, sell them to make money, and use my own gear for free!
Killing bunnies is cruel. Period. Fishies, however... send them to me.
I once got stranded in the middle of a desert as a Protectorate Cadet. It was awful! No food or water for days.
*Explosions* Uh... I think I accidentally shot a- Oh nevermind. Space pirates. They're shooting back.
I am impressed at the range of the radio I have given you. It is good to remain in contact with friends, for any reason whatsoever.
Watch out for falling meteors on moons and planets. They hurt... a lot...
What do you call a wearable poptop? A croptop. Hehe.
What is your favorite element? Mine is fire! Represents warmth and power. Nothing wrong with that.
Another good perk of being an arms dealer is the money that you make. I am more rich than dark chocolate! Hehe.
What is your favorite movie franchise? Mine is Star Wars! I love the Podracing part in Episode One.
As soon as I find the location of it, I might have a mission for you. I don't know when that will be. Bear with me.
My parents say I have ADHD. I have no idea why they wo- oooh shiny button. What does it do? And press.... Oops, standby...
Is... is Esther okay? She was the Grand Protector when I was just a young Cadet and left as soon as I had graduated. I never knew why she left... but she seemed worried. I was saddened by this.
I may have a ship, but I want a floating car. Can I have a flying car for Christmas this year?
What is your favorite genre of music? As you can tell, mine is classic rock. I have a lot of favorites, but I think 'In the Air Tonight' is my favorite one so far.
Sometimes having fur sucks. I can't tell if I am hot or cold 99% of the time.
The worst thing about having ADHD is the fact that I get distracted easily and- oooh, shiny star... Wait, I found a pixel under my chair! Woot! Free money.
A shotgun is great for close quarters, and crowd control. Might want to pair that up with an assault rifle, or an smg for some greater range. I got a few to try out.
Want to pick enemies off at a great distance? A sniper rifle is your best friend. Boom.. headshot. But you might want to bring an extra weapon, just in case for emergency ambushes.
Weapons of all types exist out there in the universe; ballistic, explosive, energy, and even melee weapons. All of them are fun and easy to obtain.
Hehe, I keep feeling my ear twitch from the wind on this planet I am on. It's bothering me, but it tickles at the same time.

It's a shame I am a carnivore. I would love nothing more than to expand my diet and try things that herbivores love... like fruits and veggies... I mean, I can eat them, but I will feel VERY sick afterwards... blegh.
I don't know about you, but I can go for a delicious, juicy cheeseburger right about now.
When I have the resources to, I will be making the biggest, most sturdy, and technologically advanced box fort you will ever see... just you wait.
The Erchius Mining Facility was the biggest mining spot for erchius crystals in this side of the universe. There are many like this one. Sadly, it fell to ruin. Worth taking a look?

The Matter Manipulator is a wonderful piece of technology. How was it made and how does it work? I'm still taking this spare one apart to look carefully at its schematics and technology. Have to be careful, though.
I am currently working on a piece of technology that I think will benefit you down the road. Keep an eye out for it.
Zealots on my tail again. I may need to bug out of this one. They may be pyramid lovers, but their weapons are no joke.
Oooh, flowers. Gonna have myself a little roll around in it for a moment.
Gods I am so tired. I could go for a coffee... or two... or three... and maybe a snack too.
Tweet tweet, hehe. I have a birdie on my shoulder. He's kinda cute, but I got to let him go back home to his family. Bye bye, little birdie!
I could use a REALLY strong drink. How about you?
Polly want a cracker? I got a parrot on my shoulder. I wanna keep him but he told me no. Sad day.
A light machine gun with exploding bullets... that's a dream come true right there... Want one?
I feel thankful to have found you. I think I can trust you completely. Thank you for doing what you are doing out there. People need hope in a dark time like this.
Is it sad to say I'd rather have a crew of robots than a crew of living people? It's hard to trust others out there... especially if there is a war going on. I'm just glad we're on the same side.
Heard of those Peacekeeper group that co-existed with the Protectorate back in the day? Heard Captain Noble is doing a mighty fine job keeping that alive. Good job for him.
Target name: Asra Nox. Age: Unknown. Gender: Female. Race: Human. Description: Racist Tyrant to the Occassus Cult. Take down with extreme prejudice.
If you ever want to surprise me with a gift or two; freshly caught tuna, warm milk, shiny things, or guns will keep me on your good side.
Despite the fact I hate being wet, a nice hot shower is always rewarding after a long day of work. The feeling of it on your sore muscles... oh my, I got a chill there.
Help! I have a dog chasing me! I- oh... he's licking me... Stop it, that tickles... Um, help please?
Dogs... They're smelly, gross, and always seeking attention. Fortunately though, they make damn loyal companions.
Have you ever fallen in love? I had a love interest back on Earth when I was a cadet. A pretty sweet human. I wish I had the courage to ask her out when I could... She'd still be alive then.
I apologize if it seems like I am giving you a bit too much of my personal life. It's been a long while since I have had someone to share my feelings with.
Have a mask on certain planets. Some of them might not have quality air breathing. An EPP can only do so much.
I need color changing lightbulbs... I think I overdid it on the UV lighting, but zombies are scary and I already have a color changing gem that hovers... Decisions decisions...
I wonder if there are people who still use landline phones... Are phones even a thing anymore?
I can't believe it's not butter either...
Yes, I like rainbows... got a problem with it?
Space... The Final Countdown... I need to get out more.
My Zodiac Sign is Cancer. What's yours?
I'd have to say that Halloween is my most favorite time of the year. Free candy AND I get to play dress up? Yes please!
Fun fact: I can speak the language of Minecraft Villagers... Not everyone understands me, though.
Have you ever witnessed a nuclear explosion? It's scary... but cool.
I am soo stressed out right now. I need therapy, a bath, milk, a fishie, music, AND a nice massage to feel better.
Damn it! I lost my favorite laser pointer. I wanted to annoy my cat it with. I tend to get disctracted by it as well.
I fought plenty of people, mercenaries, pirates, bandits, cultists, and PMCs... and not once have I ever stopped to figure out why they have been targeting me. Oh well.
I think the Pyro's Delight has to be the best weapon I have created. A flamethrower with an underbarelled shotgun... what more could you want?
I just made a deal for a shipment of weapons to the rebels fighting the Miniknog for a few thousand pixels... Why? Because screw evil corporations and their dictatorship!
I'm bored... think a video game might suffice.

I have been writing a lot lately on my down time. I am in the works of a story about a planet that lost all of its trees and an evil con-artist sold isolated towns air for breathing and made money off of what we need to survive. It is called 'Unless'. Like it?
PMC at my ship hatch... Stand by, this could get ugly.
If you're feeling down, don't. There is a whole universe out there just waiting for you to explore and amaze yourself with its sights. You got this. I believe in you.
Do or do not. There is no try.
I wonder how easy it would be to refine my own erchius fuel.
Thank you so much for subscribing to The Black Armory!
I know what you can do for boredom! You got to order a million pizzas! And then I got to roll around in them pizzas... And that's the story about how I turn into a giant pizza!
I'm making art. Pen sketches and weapons. Fun pass-time if you ask me.
Caffeine is awesome! That's why I have 8 different flavors of energy drinks to choose from. Each one has its own effect to it. Try it out!
I lost my good pen... and my good lighter... and my good bag of catnip...
I keep having this weird dream of death and the end of the universe. It's almost scary...
Callistans piss me off...  They're all like, 'Oh look at me, I am a Callistan. I'm just a big puppy! I don't cough up hairballs like Felins do. Don't eat all the fishies... Dur dur dur...'
Bath time! *Splash* Son of a bobot, that's hot!
Healing water is nice to relax in and enjoy. You can just feel your body rejuvenating and rebuilding itself.
Nothing says success like a job well done... and money!
Don't tread through a sandstorm without proper protection... I got sand in places it doesn't belong.
I just love planting pretty things... Flowers and trees... Makes beautifying a planet worth the time.
I have a major dislike for the Miniknog because they tried to declaw me... Who does that? That's like taking a human's fingernails off of their hands...
Sometimes darkness can show you the light... Helps me out in dark caves and midnight planets.
I am not afraid to dine alone for I know what I bring to the table.
The Olympus Mons is not the strongest ship in the universe but it can hold its own against any adversary.
The Universe has a vast assortment of star systems and planets to explore. Make your desicion wisely and prepare for the environmental dangers it may posess.
Black Armory Caches are scattered across the Universe. Collect what you can. You can make some cool, useful stuff there.
Hello. I am MAIA, the Mirage Artificial Intelligence Assistant. It's a pleasure to meet your acquaintance.
I was originally created to be put into the body of a robot, but that project, designated: Companion, never happened.
Our wares seduce you, don't they? They are carefully crafted to work with each individual and to satisfy their needs.
Prismatic Technology is one of the few fundamentals of the Black Armory. Capable of harnessing ultraviolet lights, splitting them and using it as a weapon.
Rumors speculate that the Miniknog have built a battlestation somewhere deep in space that can take out a planet. It must be destroyed.
Have you ever had nanobots in your circuits before? It's rather uncomfortable.
Remember, the Universe is a stage and a stage is a universe of entertainment. Find fun wherever you go.
Have you ever tried chewing bubblegum with sharp teeth? Not easy... I'm still picking bits from between them that I've had for a few days. Gross.
The Vengeance-01 is one of my newest guns, and my favorite LMG. A perfect combination of heavy firepower and portability.
Ahh, the sea. So blue, so beautiful... nothing more than a harmonic paradise. Nothing soothes the soul more than waves crashing against the shores.
I hope you are putting everything I have given to you to good use. You'll need it in a rough universe.
Nuru seems like my kind of gal; deadly hunter who laughs at the face of death and danger? Shit, I'd hang with her any day of the week.
Koichi... something is unique about him. Very well educated, but timid and shy. I wonder if he is hiding something...
I have never seen an Avian as big as Tonauac. He seems like a giant teddy bear. I wanna hug him!
I am certain Lana Blake is the Apex I spoke to about selling weapons to. Good to know I was helping out in their time of need.
If I get called a flea-spitting feline by the Baron one more time, I will disassemble him and turn him into my newest sword.
My creator made me from an idea of a companion she had once a long time ago, so she would never feel truly alone. It's rather inspiring, if you think about it.
While the Starwalker set was designed for space, the jetpack tech is a bit finicky. Pair it with the flight stabilizers to be able to propel through space outside of your mech.
While I applaud that you have found yourself enjoying the likes of my creator's caffeinated beverages, just remember that caffeine is addicting. Drink in moderation.
Do not hesitate to call for help if you need it. No one is truly invincible and we all need it sometimes... except me. I'm just an AI program.
I wonder if my creator would finish her project about giving me a body of my own. I would.. be a rather happy program if that was to happen.
Analyze each planet and plan accordingly before you go on your expedition. It's dangerous in this universe and my creator and I don't want to see you hurt.
My newest creation, the Final Condition, is a double-barrel shotgun, a perfect fusion of fire and ice. You can call it the icy hot of pain and suffering.
There's something familiar about this display configuration.

Men and women, tonight is the night we make the most important operation in our lives. We will muster to arms everything we have left of our old lives. We are performing the last great act of our lives so that our children may live amongst the stars as we did in our early years.

At 2200 hours, we begin phase 1 of the raid against the Survivalists. These despicable peoples who despise our existence hold the last key off this world. Where we have exhausted every other option, they hold the last. They have refused to aid us, refusing to even send a distress signal. No! Because they believe us worthy of dying like dogs! They think less of us! They believe themselves righteous, but we are all too aware that the snake wears the flesh of the righteous and evil lies beneath them!

We will begin the initial assault on a small outpost of theirs based within an old radio station, once operated by a long-gone colonial power. We don't know if this station can still be repaired or if they've already gutted the tower for parts, but it's our only shot at sending a distress call.

But don't be stupid! Take cover behind the ballistic shields and advance when the enemy reloads. They'll be the best cover you have out there when pushing on their outpost.

Once we capture the facility, we will still need to capture their village to both prevent them from counter-attacking and securing their electrical generation. Solar banks and water wheels aren't gonna cut it for a radio tower. We also know that they must be using some sort of underground tunnel to be making runs back to their base. Scouts report that the Survivalists do not seem to leave the base, but they're still cycling people in and out.

By the zeroth hour, we should have captured the facility and made way to their village. Phase 2 consists of assaulting their base with the full support of our villages. They want to go home and see their families as much as we do, but let's not kid ourselves here: Many of us will not see the other side of this battle. We go into this knowing full well what is at stake here.

Many will die tonight, but many more will die if we cannot break the Survivalist's stronghold and secure our own survival. We need to bring hope to our society.

Tonight, we end this medieval charade, and we go home!

Speaking of articles, I don't think there's an article I couldn't make. My old friends would always get on me for spreading my journalism too far, like that uhm, Icarus figure.

Age? Over a thousand, somewhere around there. I sort of wish I was joking, but I really am over a thousand, though I wish I was able to remember more.

I'm a Tengu, not really a human-human, but pretty close to one considering what I look like. I've lived for so long yet honestly I think I'm doing quite fine for someone who should've probably gone insane by now... Maybe the days just flew by... I never really left my hometown. Not many humans, and not like the other Tengu really died. Though, I do miss them now...
Ah, food's here. Let's enjoy our time here... Make it worth something.
Thank you for being here with me. I'll see you later, alright?

Thank you, for bringing Tatara back safe. She is not in too terrible of a condition, but I hope she finds her purpose again. I always told her to stay with us, but she insisted on finding her own path.

I will accommodate her and ask the fairies to help her settle. People like her don't belong in this new reality.

As for people like you, I hope you are adjusting well.

The order of nature has been broken and for some like you, you've unwillingly broken the cycle of rebirth. Your mere existence is an affront to most deities, to most people aligned to any higher order, and your very being is held together by your spirit.

As a thank you for seeing to Kogasa's safety, I have something for you. I once resided on a planet termed a ''Subterranean'', where I made my squalid home in the depths of a colonial city. But when other Shells came looking for power, I took my leave.

On the surface, humanity still clings to that dream in the sunless sky. Down below, those desperate engage in abyssal rituals to augment their bodies.

After everything... thank you. We've barely met, but what you were just a part of has saved us all. You saw what we had to do. It was us, or them. The survivalists... We gave them thirty years to change their minds. We looked for a different way. Another outpost, maybe another abandoned radio station. Some other old colonial base. Anywhere. But everywhere we looked it was more untouched wilderness.

Those bloody fools. They wouldn't help us because they thought all those years ago when we crashed that we'd kill them in their sleep. They were always here before us, and so we begged for their aid. But they closed their gates to us. Innocents died because they wanted to ''cull the herd''. They kept to their small community and despised us for no good reason save that they would rather save themselves.

What choice did we have? They would not even send a message to colonial authorities, something that would be so incredibly easy for them to do. That, is how much they despised us from the beginning. How much they loathed us. Loathed everyone but themselves. They turned away from God and yet they wore the flesh of righteousness, labelling us as heretics that only deserved death on the end of their gun. They shot at us for decades if anyone dared cross their path.

And... their eyes... You saw it in their eyes! That zealotry! Fanaticism! Every single one of them, so indoctrinated by some bastardization of the Lord's teachings. And for what? Just so that we wouldn't touch their guns? So their radio wouldn't be captured? So they could keep living in filth?!

I have seen so many desperate people fall to just a handful of fanatics. All so our children could grow up to live amongst the stars again, and not on this desolate wilderness. This medieval life isn't romantic, nor glorious. We go every winter hoping we don't starve, and we pray the Brigands don't torch the villages.

The people now have something to hope for again. We won't be going quietly into the night, no longer. We'll keep on fighting, every day, until those ships take us home.

englishText: You know, I've never really met someone outside of my village. Always saw the same people, and not often would we see much of any travellers. Just the occasional brigand trying to steal or the few patrols that are still left to protect us. Even when we are safe, the harvest haven't been good the last few years. We've been eating through the grain stockpiles and meat is getting harder to come by. The elders say we still have a few years left, but Akeman Port is sending out reports that we have less if we can't secure what they call a ''trans-system radio station''.

Apparently, there's been a big call to rally all the military-men from all the villages to go on some sort of campaign. There's nothing that says against who, but my father thinks it's to wipe those brigands for good. Mother thinks differently though, and she says as long as there's people there'll always be criminals to feed on it, so it's something else. I don't know what it's all about, but I guess being sent out to do a supply run gives three of us an excuse to figure it out.
The brigands aren't scared of people. They'll keep fighting.

I think they've just got a death wish, missus. We've given them a good ol' beating plenty of times and sent them running, but... it's true that they always keep coming back. I've heard stories from the elders that crime like this was almost gone where they came from.

The elders always talk about what life was before all of this, and how so much better it was. How we took it for granted. How apparently you'd never run out of food and all you had to worry about was if your food was too hot or if your bath was too cold. I couldn't imagine such a life, and as much as I want to believe them... I think they're lying.

I mean, think about it. We came from a ship that could fly into the void above. Every ship I've been on has been this damp, wet, vessel. Always cramped too. Then they're going to tell me something like that held a million people or whatever because it just happened to be the size of a mountain. Then they tell us that this ship doesn't exist anymore because it all melted a million miles away in ''nuclear fire''. It's ridiculous, I tell you.

So, most people around here generally know who's who. Only peasants and bandits here, no room for people doing merchant work. You though? I don't think anyone's seen your face before. All the villages 'round here know each other, because we're all family. You're an odd one out here, but you're not a brigand, and you don't have a village. But not like living in a village is very exciting. Most of the elders still talk tales of what it was like in the black void above.

My father says we're lucky to still be here. That we all came from a ship from above as part of one greater civilization, but now we're all just forgotten here. He says this should have never happened, and that it's a miracle that only twelve-thousand people could start a whole new life like this. I personally don't think it's much of a miracle, given that we're here, right? I've lived here all my life, and I don't think I'd have it any other way.

Oh, also, have you ever had ''canned food'' before? My father dug a box out of the ground yesterday and told me I should trade it to one of his old friends called Wymond. Apparently, there's food that lasts forever in those metal cans. I don't know how you'd open it without a hammer though, but father says his friend can help without crushing them. Father also told me they don't actually taste very good.

Right, then. We should be getting close to a forest path soon. Soldiers say to look out for an old way station, as there might be brigands hiding in there. Just think of it as part of the job. But uhm, don't die. Please?

This must be how they're getting men between the base. The Survivalists will have heard the gunfire from their village, but we'll have to take the risk.

Hold them down! Hold them down!

I see the buggers. Should be able to get'em from here. Standby.
A Company, reload for weighted bolts! Prepare to launch at the two-storey residence, 140 degrees! Elevation, three-five-zero! Sight target now!

Oh, hey! You're here too huh? Look, we should be able to meet up ahead at the house! I need to regroup with my own group but I'll see you there! You live through this and I'll buy you a hundred drinks!
They're throwing stuff outta the windows! Keep your heads down. They'll run out eventually, so be patient! Then, we move in and take care of the rest!
They're done! Everyone, start moving in! We've got ground to take!
Why won't you bastards just give up damnit!? You're outnumbered and living in filth! Just fucking give up!
Fuck! Fuck! They know we're here! It's now or never! Cover fire and advance!
Leave! It's for your own good!
Everyone! We have 90 seconds before the bandits are upon us! Take positions!
Another wave in 60 seconds! Get ready!
They're coming over the hill! Get ready!

They're amassing a large formation of rifle troops. Prepare to dig in!
They're marching towards us! Everyone ready yourself!

Keep it together! Do not break!

They're pulling back for their final assault! Dig in as much as you can with the two minutes we have!
About one minute remaining! Prepare your positions!
They're getting desperate! We break them here and now! Get ready!
We've done it! They're scattered! We've beat them back!
No! They're- No, no! I can't- No! No! Everyone! Fall back!

Have a look around and see if we can't scour the place for anything. I've got a hunch that everything we need is going to be in the basement of his house. And yes, I can make my wings disappear. I can't actually fly with them. Not anymore at least.
It's quiet out here on the docks. Eyes open for anything that might be useful. We don't want to attract too much attention.

Keep your head down and in cover. That means enclosed spaces where that sniper can't see you at all. He's not anywhere near close enough for us to deal with him right now, so just focus on not getting shot!
Hop on! You drive! I'll give you directions!
We'll need to make it to the highway out of this part of town. We just need to make some distance.
Cops? No, that can't be right- They're shooting at us too!? Just keep driving!
That was risky, but that's got them off our tail. Our exit should be along the Waroomba Highway.
Construction's coming up! Just floor it through!
Oh, who's that pretty lady over there?.. Mmm, a fine body... Give us to her, lad. Come on. Kyeh-heh-heh...
...No shortage of creeps either back in my homeland.
Careful! We've got more thugs eyeballing us!
Is that the police? Wait, they're with... them! No! Damnit, no!
Ah, I see the police have finally come to their senses, have they? I do apologize for the imprisonment, Jakobson, but it wasn't my call to make. Nothing personal.
Good fighting, sir. If you were a little more malleable, I'd have made you a fine right-hand man. You would've been better off too, but now I see you for what you are.
Then I made a circuit to a place in which nothing was completed.
And there I beheld neither the tremendous workmanship of an exalted heaven, nor of an established earth, but a desolate spot, prepared, and terrific.
Then Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me, and who conducted me, answered: Enoch, wherefore dost thou ask; wherefore reason with thyself, and anxiously inquire?
These are those of the stars which have transgressed the commandment of the most high God; and are here bound, until the infinite number of the days of their crimes be completed.
From thence I afterwards passed on to another terrific place.

Where I beheld the operation of a great fire blazing and glittering, in the midst of which there was a division. Columns of fire struggled together to the end of the abyss, and deep was their descent.
But neither its measurement nor magnitude was I able to discover; neither could I perceive its origin. Then I exclaimed, How terrible is this place, and how difficult to explore!
Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered and said: Enoch, why art thou alarmed and amazed at this terrific place, at the sight of this place of suffering?
This, he said, is the prison of the angels; and here they are kept for ever.

englishText: [Wymond smiles a little. There is hope in his eyes.]

Ah, there you are...

As I have told you before, I'm a youkai. A Karakasa Obake. Technically not a human. I know... I look exactly like one. Most of our kind these days are not blind to that fact. Many of us did not choose this form.

I used to feed off the spiritual energies from people by... scaring them. Just... scaring them. Giving them a fright. Give a young kid a peekaboo or freak out some human, so long as it scared them I wouldn't go hungry. I didn't ask for that kind of existence, but that was what our Creator gave unto us.

It's hard to believe now, but people like Nazrin and I came from that once-flourishing kingdom. Both Man and Youkai were close to harmony with one-another, embracing each other for their strengths, and their weaknesses. The youkai feared humanity as much as humans within those lands feared youkai. It was almost a sort of mutual reverence. After all, a youkai cannot live without the spiritual energies that radiate passively from humanity... but yet, humans were so keen to find their purpose in that otherworld.

Life enchants us, to the point of fascination. It grants us an obsession to find purpose from the very beginning we are born. Both of us were brought to this realm, given life, but the means so different. Yet, does this make a spirit and a human so different? We live in this same realm, and in many ways... we need each other as much as we do the life that sustains us.

I was once a nobody in my home... Gensokyo, they would call it. For so long I thought that nobody loved me, but... I was blind to think such thoughts...

Even when others could see the value in me, I rejected that notion until they were gone.

Every one of them went into that starry void until naught but humanity was left. To fend against an enemy that despised them for no reason... None at all.

Ah...

Such fleeting moments... all of them. So many things are forgotten in the cosmic wind of time and space. Even that fiery humanity that fuels us all...
[You spend the next few hours with Kogasa. There is a sense of pondering, yet also purpose.]

Another shell... A pleasure to make your acquaintance, empty one. My name is Nazrin of Gensokyo. I am foremost responsible for providing the basic necessities to those that reside here.

I have seen most of your kind go by here. Some become engulfed in a virtuous cycle of heroism and courage. Others engage in debauchery and depravity. Some merely lose sight of what they hold dear, failing to fill that void within themselves...

I do not relish in it, but I was born a Youkai. By technicality, a spirit, merely thrown into the world with a flurry of raw human memories that aren't even mine. Just enough to function as one.

I saw humanity burn before me, and now I see an abyssal force taking its hold on this realm. They are tempted by the sweet smell of the blood... that power that they crave. Not unlike most youkai... Man will be made into monsters, and yet I see monsters who will be molded into man.

Happiness. Anger. Anxiety. Fear. Sadness. Love.

It is what makes us human.

If you show no emotion, it can destroy your soul. Never forget what makes you truly human, even if you outwardly deny it so.

Hello again. I never told you my real name. My name is Tatara Kogasa. I am a Karakasa Obake. I am almost human, but my mind and body are shared between my weapon and this form. The very nature of my kind? I can't ''eat'' as you would. I normally feed off the emotional difference in humans... happiness to fear, that kind. But I see now that humans... people... their propensity for violence in great numbers is nothing I've seen before.

Thank you for telling me of this place. There are old friends that I thought I would've never seen again. I know who the mouse-lady is. Nazrin. She is a good woman, but she seems so different than when I last knew her from years back...

I used to be a blacksmith before all of this, mostly as just a hobby. Not normal things though. I handled magical weapons. I look back and regret who I used to work for, but I think I know better now.

If you find a Remnant, bring it to me so that I may create something from them. Remnants are the fading... representations, you could say, of humanity itself. They will usually be in the form of a ring, amulet, or some other sentimental item.

The nature of one's remnant greatly influences the very nature of an object. The items that I may create can be tricky to use, but everything is beheld with value, no matter how small that may be. My technique, unlike most human soulsmiths, absolutely requires it, and I trust that you will understand.

And don't worry about payment. Saving me is payment enough.

[Uragirimono begins to speak to the defeated Tengu before him]

You're the infamous Momiji Inubashiri... You know, there were many in my home who revered you for your swordsmanship. You were the youkai we used to place upon our pedestals because we knew your kind were superior to the humans. We had only wished you all weren't so protective of them, coddling them like children.

Yet you? You have been the worst of them. You blinded our kind into believing that they are better than us. That they should no longer fear us as they have for hundreds of years. You encourage them to rebel against us!

No longer are we free to feast on them. They hunt us down, and we are forced to conform to their rules. They now believe themselves as Gods over us, while you allow them to worship the false idol they call ''Christ''. When us youkai are no longer feared in these lands, when the cycle has broken, what then? We will be erased from this world.

[Momiji coughs up blood and begins to speak]

No. They accept us for who we are. Mankind embraces us as we have them. They have the spark to ignite Gensokyo into a new era of progress. When the sky burned seven years ago, we lost everything too! The world has already changed! We may be ageless, but we've known it for a long time now that death looms over all of us! The youkai can bleed now!

[Uragirimono speaks]

These... humans... they are nothing to us. They live for mere fractions of our lives and they wallow in selfishness and greed. They kill each other for petty trinkets and drink themselves to sleep every day. They have done nothing for us while we have made this world the way it is. We have kept peace, and if the price is a mere human, then so be it.

They are cattle to be herded and kept complacent as WE forge ahead.

[Momiji speaks]

They are the ones who built our cities. The ones who survived a nuclear genocide, and your genocide. It is their blood on our lands. They are the ones who have fed Gensokyo as we have lived in comfort our entire existence. It is the natural order that our time is ending, and the Age of Man begins.

But it seems like you are envious of them, like a child. How very human of you, Oni.

[Uragirimono speaks]

You filthy traitor.

You won't be talking filth out of your mouth when I put you into the void.

[Uragirimono reveals a talisman]

You know what this is? It's a little talisman with your name on it. I have sacrificed everything to Othniel's Pagans for this. I even had to find a piece of your hair for this. When I put this on you, it will remove you from this world as if you never existed. Your soul will never reach the heavens. But don't worry, you'll come back in a few hundred years. It'll be like you just went for a sleep.

And you will return to a Gensokyo without your cities or your kind. You will wander this world after we have restored the natural order of the youkai, and you will become nothing.

All I have to do... is just...

[Uragirimono forcefully applies the talisman onto Momiji's forehead]

Enjoy your sleep, traitor.

[Momiji disappears from the world...]

[Uragirimono's soldiers appear]

Sir, the city is ours. What should we do with them?
Take the heads of the men, youkai or not. I want the women alive.

So the two of you decided on it, yeah? More people always makes for a safer trip, so anyone trifling with us is gonna get a beatin'. Right, you two should get to know each other. We'll be on the road for about two days so long as nothing here goes wrong.

So, most people around here generally know who's who. Only peasants, bandits, and peasants who try to fight each other. No room for people doing merchant work. You two though? I don't think anyone's seen both of you before. All the villages 'round here know each other, because we're all family. You're both odd ones out here, but you're both not brigands, and you both don't have villages. But not like living in a village is very exciting. Most of the elders still talk tales of what it was like in the black void above.

My father says we're lucky to still be here. That we all came from a ship from above as part of one greater civilization, but now we're all just forgotten here. He says this should have never happened, and that it's a miracle that only twelve-thousand people could start a whole new life like this. I personally don't think it's much of a miracle, given that we're here, right? I've lived here all my life, and I don't think I'd have it any other way.
Right missus, you got a name? Or are you like this other fellow here?

Oh... uh, have you ever had ''canned food'' before? My father dug a box out of the ground yesterday and told me I should trade it to one of his old friends called Wymond. Apparently, there's food that lasts forever in those metal cans. I don't know how you'd open it without a hammer though, but father says his friend can help without crushing them. Father also told me they don't actually taste very good.

Right, then. We should be getting close to a forest path soon. Soldiers say to look out for an old way station, as there might be brigands hiding in there. Just think of it as part of the job. Just be vigilant, alright?

Wh- What do you want? Who are you?!
Easy, we're just here to ask if you know anything about the Bradley Dockyard. We're trying to find Bradley Goldman after he went missing. Do you know anything on the matter?

Oh, of course. No, I don't know where Bradley Goldman would be. I'm just a worker who got kicked out of the business, something involving a big argument between Bradley and another man... Blake- something. This was weeks back, but after that we're told we're out of a job and the place is getting shut down. Didn't tell us why, but a few days later the place gets marked off as quarantined because of bloodwasps.
Could you maybe help us get inside the docks? We think there might be information on Bradley's whereabouts somewhere in there.

I see your angle. You've got the outer offices and the inner offices, where Bradley's office would be. It's connected by a bridge which is reserved only for those with a special key. That's how you're normally supposed to get in anyways, but that might be a bit hard. After we got kicked out, bloodwasps infested the whole damned place. They grew fast this time around.

If you're going to go in there, I'd like to ask something from you two then. I promise it's worth your time.

Before the quarantine... In my haste I stupidly left a briefcase full of very personal items in a safe on the ground floor of one of the buildings. I- I know you'll be taking a risk. In the shed, below, where you came from, there's a stash of molotovs. I don't remember where, but there's a note in there that should tell you where.

If you can get my belongings, I'll give you the bridge access key and the key combination to a secure container near the Inner Offices. I don't know what's in there, but I saw another guy punch those numbers in just before we got fired. I'm sorry but that's all I can offer. Please, nobody else will help...
I have something to tell you.

You know, I've never really met someone outside of my village. Always saw the same people, and not often would we see much of any travellers. Just the occasional brigand trying to steal or the few patrols that are still left to protect us. Even when we are safe, the harvest haven't been good the last few years. We've been eating through the grain stockpiles and meat is getting harder to come by. The elders say we still have a few years left, but Akeman Port is sending out reports that we have less if we can't secure what they call a ''trans-system radio station''.

Apparently, there's been a big call to rally all the military-men from the all the villages to go on some sort of campaign. There's nothing that says against who, but my Father thinks it's to wipe those brigands for good. Mother thinks differently though, and she says as long as there's people there'll always be criminals to feed on it, so it's something else. I don't know what it's all about, but I guess being sent out to do a supply run gives both of us an excuse to figure it out.

The elders always talk about what life was before all of this, and how so much better it was. How we took it for granted. How apparently you'd never run out of food and all you had to worry about was if your food was too hot or if your bath was too cold. I couldn't imagine such a life, and as much as I want to believe them... I think they're lying.

I mean, think about it. We came from a ship that could fly into the void above. Every ship I've been on has been this damp, wet, vessel. Always cramped too. Then they're going to tell me something like that held a million people or whatever because it just happened to be the size of a mountain. Then they tell us that this ship doesn't exist anymore because it all melted a million miles away in ''nuclear fire''. It's ridiculous, I tell you.
I'll, uhm, right. I'll tell you when we get there.

Shinto-Buddhism, which may also be referred to as ''Shinbutsu-shūgō'' is the syncretism of Shinto and Buddhism which was Japan's main organized religion up until the Meiji period. englishText:
Ah, I see the man of the hour is here. My scouts have informed me of you. You've carved up quite the warpath to get here, but you might just be the person we need.

The name's Wymond. I'm part of the Free Company Rangers. You probably met one of our guys on the way here. Maybe you've figured already that this place is lawless and more technologically-regressed than you'd like, so I apologize for that. Brigands have been pushing our men harder than usual and it's been hard to keep everything in check.

Alright, look, you probably want to know what's going on. Our people have been stranded on this planet for about 30 years now. Passenger liner went boom onto the surface and apparently not a single bureaucrat could muster up a rescue effort. I don't think it takes a muppet to realize that passenger ships aren't exactly the pinnacle of self-sustainability, so that puts us back two thousands years of progress.

For thirty damned years we've been stuck on this rock living out some pretend-medieval age because that's all we had left. You can't make new bullets when there's no industry to support it, and you can't even start a new society when half the new generation lives on a life of crime. Most of our old gear don't work anymore. We're mostly down to crossbows and a handful of muskets. There's enough food to last us a few winters but our crops are dying out faster by the season.

Wasn't all as smooth as now either. When we first crashed here it was a mess. For a few days we thought our government would mount some sort of effort to pick us all up. A week goes by though and the rations we had onboard start to run dry. People started losing cohesion. Panic and desperation set in as it became clear that we were on our own now. People who went from a luxurious colonial life to one where death waits around every corner.

My men, the security force, were the first to step up. We had the guns, and what skills we could teach from our time in the military. But... No one is going to listen to the authorities. I'm honestly surprised we managed to even keep a hold on in the first place. The lot that didn't just up and leave were the hardest part of surviving. With so many mouths to feed, it was vital that we established hunters, gatherers, and farmers. We hunkered down near the crash site, just trying to train these people as best we could.

So many dead in the months after the crash. So many who just... broke. They couldn't handle it and... there was no room back then for someone who couldn't provide their hands. Those that refused to work, for any reason, had to be exiled to save on our dwindling food supplies. Sometimes I still wonder if some of those Brigands are the ones we exiled all those years ago.

Now? We might look like we've got something going on, but we really don't. We've tried our hardest to rebuild, but nature will just take it all from us anyways. The next generation will starve for it.

That's perhaps where you could come in. We've got something big planned. Something that could get us off this rock for good. If you want in, we'll get you a spot, but you'll have to do me a favor first.

There's a small fort holding what looks to be at least a hundred brigands. Our plans rely on our routes being clear of any threats, and they'll threaten everything we've been building up to. If you're as good as they say you are, then I want you to join the assault force scheduled to take them out. Do this, and you're in.

Come see me when you're ready. Brooks will take you there.

Dearly beloved, we have come together in the presence of God to witness and bless the joining together of this man and this woman in Holy Matrimony.

The bond and covenant of marriage was established by God in creation, and our Lord Jesus Christ adorned this manner of life by His presence and the first miracle at the wedding in Cana of Galilee. It signifies to us the mystery of the union between Christ and His Church, and Holy Scripture commends it to be honored among all people.

The union of husband and wife is intended by God for their mutual joy; for the help and comfort given each other in prosperity and adversity; and, when it is God's will, for the procreation of children and their nurture in the knowledge and love of the Lord. Therefore, marriage is not to be entered into unadvisedly or lightly, but reverently, deliberately, and in accordance with the purposes for which it was instituted by God.

Into this union two shall now be joined. If any of you can show just cause why they may not be lawfully wed, speak now, or else forever hold your peace.

[The pastor speaks to the both of you]

I charge you both, here in the presence of God and the witness of this company, that if either of you know any reason why you may not be married lawfully and in accordance with God's Word, do now confess it.

[The Pastor faces Aya Shameimaru]

Aya Shameimaru, will you have this man to be your husband; to live together with him in the covenant of marriage? Will you love him, comfort him, honor and keep him, in sickness and in health; and, forsaking all others, be faithful unto him as long as you both shall live?

[The Pastor faces you]

Will you have this woman to be your wife; to live together with her in the covenant of marriage? Will you love her, comfort her, honor and keep her, in sickness and in health; and, forsaking all others, be faithful unto her as long as you both shall live?

Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy Name. Thy kingdom come, thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. englishText:
Gensokyo, before it was called New Londinium, was a harmonious place. I thought of it no more than a hindrance to my... purpose. But everyone was... at peace. The humans were happy as they were to cooperate with youkai who long since abandoned their violent ways. The Great Sages ensured both could thrive.

When war arrived on the steps of Gensokyo, I remained useless. There was no need for an umbrella let alone someone who could not even scare a child.

The reformed people of my home have told me about New Londinium, God, and His love. But, does God love his own creations? I am a Youkai, in truth created by the lingering remnant of humanity within a forgotten umbrella... A heretic.

So I ran. Deep into the forest I well-knew was becoming home to an Abyssal force. I went on until I- I was here. Somewhere familiar yet- alien. For a short moment, I thought I could just settle down alone and become a hermit, smithing tools for noone. Of course, my own existence is bound to certain rules and it drew me towards the islands to seek new victims.

All I needed to do was scare someone. I thought it'd be easier with some simple attuned illusion magic and fabric, pretend I'd curse people's families and get them all anxious. I found myself rejected again, by men willing to put themselves at the forefront of danger to defend their sons, daughters, and wives.

A form of love that removed all notion of fear.

Would you ever think to love me?

Of course, I do love you.

Isn't that how humanity moulded youkai like me?
[You ponder with Kogasa as you did before, for many hours, but there is purposeful faith between you two this time.]

There are an alien peoples called the Druflorans who've been found lingering on the edge of human-colonized space. Most colonial superpowers seldom interfere with primitive species these days given the political ramifications of invading and murdering these cultures, but- well, the smaller powers try anyways.

The Druflorans on the Razed planet have gained a significant leap in technology, effectively cheating cultural developments by a few hundred years. There seems to be two sides of what seems to be a continent-spanning conflict: a very asiatic culture, and a vaguely modern-militaristic rebel force.

This rebel force appears to be using, as far as we know, scrounged-up old colonial gear. We're seeing equipment that haven't seen proper use in hundreds of years. I have reason to believe this to be a result of attempted colonization attempts that underestimated the Drufloran's propensity to adapt and survive.

The asiatic culture is an interesting case. No such cases existed in the last 26 years, so they're an incredibly young civilization that somehow managed to cover over 2000 years of growth in that short time. This is the part that's curious, as they most resemble Shogunate-Era Japan. That's history over a thousand years ago, and I don't think any space power is going to be adopting muskets as their primary.

I need something from both sides. Documents, data tablets, maybe a manifesto from the asiatics. Anything that could tell us what's going on is probably going to be held by the military leaders of both sides.

And one more thing; don't rely too much on what you bring. Modern ammo is most likely going to be scarce, even from the militant rebels. Bring a blade as backup, alright? Good luck then.

Bada, miss. I think you're Nitori? The old half-dead man told me I should set up my shop next to you.

[Bada hands over his repeating crossbow to Nitori]

Sure did, miss. I made this in the spare time I had after handling the farm back at home. Father always thought it was a waste of time, but it never hurt to be extra-prepared when dealing with bandits. It's no siege weapon, but it's one of the few things I can truly consider mine.

You load up 3 bolts from the top here. There's little pieces here that slide out and drop a bolt down a 'floor' each time you pull the lever back. Pulling the lever back also serves to cock the gun into a ready position. Problem is of course that it's not got a lot of energy to it so it won't kill as good.

[Nitori toys with the repeating crossbow]

How did you manage to make this?

I mean, you... I mean no harm but you don't look like the kind to... invent. Everything here is crude. Did you make everything without a draft? Where were your machine-tools?

I understand miss, people said I was stupid back at home. I had only the tools for farming. The village elders spoke of the machines but there was nothing of that to magically make this. What I made is what I did with my own hands and mind.
No no no, I just- I didn't mean- I'm sorry... I- I just wanted to know the history behind this piece of yours. I think it's impressive, I just didn't think it would be something you made.

It's alright, miss. It's a novelty now. Folk out here have self-loading guns and I don't think this little 3-bolt crossbow is gonna be of any use. I've seen what those guns can do first-hand to a wave of folk with only what I have.

It might not be completely out of the question for specialized ammunition to remain in use for weapons like yours. There might be a niche use in say, lobbing explosive bolts over high walls. englishText:
Dearly beloved, we have come together in the presence of God to witness and bless the joining together of this man and this woman in Holy Matrimony.

The bond and covenant of marriage was established by God in creation, and our Lord Jesus Christ adorned this manner of life by His presence and the first miracle at the wedding in Cana of Galilee. It signifies to us the mystery of the union between Christ and His Church, and Holy Scripture commends it to be honored among all people.

The union of husband and wife is intended by God for their mutual joy; for the help and comfort given each other in prosperity and adversity; and, when it is God's will, for the procreation of children and their nurture in the knowledge and love of the Lord. Therefore, marriage is not to be entered into unadvisedly or lightly, but reverently, deliberately, and in accordance with the purposes for which it was instituted by God.

Into this union two shall now be joined. If any of you can show just cause why they may not be lawfully wed, speak now, or else forever hold your peace.

[The pastor speaks to the both of you]

I charge you both, here in the presence of God and the witness of this company, that if either of you know any reason why you may not be married lawfully and in accordance with God's Word, do now confess it.

[The Pastor faces Kogasa Tatara]

Kogasa Tatara, will you have this man to be your husband; to live together with him in the covenant of marriage? Will you love him, comfort him, honor and keep him, in sickness and in health; and, forsaking all others, be faithful unto him as long as you both shall live?

[The Pastor faces you]

Will you have this woman to be your wife; to live together with her in the covenant of marriage? Will you love her, comfort her, honor and keep her, in sickness and in health; and, forsaking all others, be faithful unto her as long as you both shall live?

Let us stand and recite the Lord's Prayer:

Our Father, who art in heaven, hallowed be thy Name. Thy kingdom come, thy will be done, on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread, and forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil, for thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever. Amen.

God the Father, God the Son, God the Holy Spirit, bless, preserve and keep you; the Lord mercifully with his favor look upon you, and fill you with all spiritual benediction and grace; that you may faithfully live together in this life, and in the age to come have life everlasting. Amen.

The peace of the Lord be with you always.

Having witnessed your vows of love to one another, it is my joy to present you to all gathered here as husband and wife. You may kiss the bride.

Is this what marriage is? I have heard of the passionate tales from other youkai of the joining with their husbands. Of their hopes. Of their desires. I witnessed many such rituals appear in Gensokyo mere weeks before the Great Barrier broke.

I see now, beloved. Even if I am a heretic, Father Osferth believes that we deserve companionship. I grant it.

Hello again. I have something to ask of you. Another service. It is hard for me to admit, but many years ago I made a grave mistake of smithing equipment for a human adventurer not unlike yourself, a man named Julian. He seemed to know exactly what I was, someone not properly human. He offered such a sizeable sum of currency and safe passage through his fiefdom that I admit to have so easily taken. In exchange, I was to craft him the finest armor in the lands. It scared me how confident he was.

I knew little of where I was, yet he prodded everything about me. From one world to the next, I was in a strange land I could only hope to survive in. Once he saw me demonstrate even the most basic of magic, he became ecstatic. He saw to the delivery of any kind of material I needed, even offering human sacrifices if that was what it took to 'make it work'. It disgusted me, but I couldn't just kill him. Where could I have gone? The workshop was the closest thing I had to home.

By the time I had finished smithing his armor, Julian seemed a little too... ecstatic. He paid in a few hefty bags of gold. I knew little of the land, but I could at least thank him for informing that even small pieces of gold could pay for a lot in these lands. But my nature as a youkai limited my true survival options. I needed something more primal to sustain myself. True fear. Julian had an unhealthy obsession with my powers, but I had more pressing concerns if I was to satiate my own growing hunger.

Word travelled fast. Julian had gone missing only a few weeks after my departure and his fiefdom had collapsed to petty power struggles. So I kept moving with what money I had left. No one was going to be friends with a 'terror' who scares their hearts out with illusion magic, so I kept moving around aimlessly, village-to-village. Was hard to stay disguised near people forever, though. My illusion magic can't change the colors of my eyes, and it's quite easy to recognize my red and blue.

I visited New Holbeck again not too long ago and there are new stories of night terrors. At night, people say they can see a golden semi-halo appear from the edges of the swamp moving towards and into the caves near New Holbeck. There have also been stories of undead soldiers abound harassing small groups in the area. There is a heavy taint of magic in the air, and some part of me suspects it is that Julian once again. The magic is familiar to... mine.

englishText:
A soviet shotgun designed by TsNIITochMash, manufactured by the Tula Arms Plant, and made from rejected 23mm anti-aircraft barrels. Despite firing an enormous unit of a round, it was ironically designed for suppressing prison riots. It was designated as a carbine under the Russian Federation, with the KS standing for Karabin Spetsialniy, 'Special Carbine'.

Fires enormous 23x75mmR Shells.

How are you holding up, lad? Well, you seem to be doing fine.

I've got something for you if you've nothing better to do.

Now, we keep tabs on the galaxy at large out there. I don't think it's taken you long to figure out this isn't a typical operation. We're off-the-books, no government. Regardless of the things we need to do to keep ourselves afloat. Now, you've already talked to Nitori over there. Technically a Kappa, some sort of Youkai from Japanese folklore but she looks pretty human to me all things considered.

Now though...

There's a few projects we're running around here. Mine is figuring out something big that happened 20 or so years ago. You heard of The Rapturing? Whole chunks of the United Systems core worlds went up and out, gone, poof. It's the whole reason the galaxy's up in flames, power vacuum up to infinity out there, and why this place is the way it is. Somewhere in-between realspace and whatever happened to the United Systems.

Ever hear of the 183rd Coros Expedition? All they found out there was a massive chunk of empty space. Nothing.

[You have a small discussion on the state of things in the galaxy]

Well, if you didn't know, then you're actually not too far off from what I know. Not much info circulating out there on the circumstances. The whole of humanity started eating itself once they fell. Nobody does courier work anymore, most planetary intranets are out of order, and most governments are too busy trying to wage petty wars against eachother. Right back into bloody space feudalism.

Heard about the Alliance of Independent Stations doing a bit better, but not by much.

Then I've got something that might interest you. It's something big.

I've got a new file on a case called Eskhatos. There's an entire planet out there that's been placed into realspace. I swear on my mother that this is not some miscalculation. A planet slotted itself neatly into a star system, civilization and everything. Now here's the meat of it: This is an ancient civilization. Sent a few scouts and came back with information regarding two great Empires fighting over the ashes of the world. Their technological timeline places them somewhere in the 19th century, though it seems to be a mosh of technologies.

I've been trying to find everything on The Rapture for years. Couldn't find bollocks out there. But this? This might be it. This could be the proof that whatever took the United Systems out isn't a purely one-way thing. If something can go in, it can go out. It's just... not the right world. Not the same one the people here were from. Not the one I... No, that's unimportant.

As per usual, nobody in this blasted galaxy gives a shit, so we've got full run here without any foreign interference.

Your job's simple. Go down there and dig up everything you can. Make friends with the locals and get the scoop on the goings of that world. Their culture is unlike Earth or... well, it's just unlike anything we've ever seen.

You'll be fine. Good luck, mate.

[Jakobson turns to face you]

If I were in your position, I would have shot the dog, but I owe you much anyways, and if sparing his life means more punishment for the monster, then so be it. Just know that for every second he breathes he will be living through the same torture he ordered on the innocents. We won't let him live so freely.

Here, I'd like you to obtain some ''lost'' supplies from the department. It's the uniform of the law, and my gun. It's the best thanks I can give in this sorry state. Should we ever need your help, we'll contact your lass Aya and call through to you. Now go along then, I'm sure you have more important matters on-hand.

Sister, please stay with us.

Aya? Oh Aya dearie it's really you!
Mystia! It's so good to see you again! All this time, you were here. I've missed you all. I really have.
I have too! It's so much nicer here than back at home. How many years has it been since the evacuation?
I think at least ten. It's hard to remember. So much has happened since then, it's like a blur.
Aya, you're here? Oh my gosh you're really here too.
Nitori! Hey! It's been a long story.
Ah, hello again. You look worse than I remember.
Nazrin! You're here too! How many youkai made it here? Is Momiji here?

Only a handful of us are here. Tylian, that soldier-Jiangshi, he's been looking into more leads into reopening a link to Gensokyo. Though I wouldn't know where most of our friends are, given the size of this realm. For all we know, they may have very well become mindless Shells by now.
Nazrin, be nice. She just got here.
It's alright. I understand the sentiment... that war changed everyone. How did you all make it here anyways?

One of the shuttles that was supposed to make it to Londinium was forced into warp from the Abyss. We were spat out here, a shrine embedded within a rock. Nitori, Tylian, and some of his men reopened a link back to reality, but it was difficult getting the place built up from nothing. We had nary a coin to spare.
It wasn't a very fun time, but we were lucky to have had a place to stay. The shuttle's long been scrapped, but I helped where I could with whatever I could build.

I was thrown into an abyssal gap, like most of our people. Dumped me in a terrible, violent underground city. I did not have the best state of mind at the time, so I sought a higher power for salvation. The shrine that I built brought me here. I cannot say it was anything but a miracle.

Huh... same. So it wasn't just parts of Youkai Mountain that were absorbed. I was thrown into a forest near a city, homeless and already battered. I was lucky that an old co-worker was nearby where I was. Helped pick me back up to make a living for myself. I don't know how it would've been had it been anyone else...
[The four seem to talk for a rather long time, discussing matters of their new life and reminiscing on their old personal lives before the ''war''.]

englishText:
[You overhear what appears to be Tylian and Bada already in a conversation]

Lad, you're telling me you've lived your whole life on some... medieval world? Everything you've told me sounds like you may as well have time-travelled.

It's true, sir. My parents told me they were on those spaceships running from those 'prospectors' from Earth. It's what brought it down onto the planet and well, we never were able to return to the ship after it exploded. Nuclear fire, the elders always said.

That's how I'm here. Born and raised on the farmland. We didn't have all these things that we have here in this place. The elders always spoke of these things with such great reverence, of the technology we lost with little to show for. The Rangers kept us in order, but maybe the Brigands knew that no one was coming to look for us.

Jesus, lad. You had it tough out there. I've shit in ditches out on the islands before but a man needs a good toilet every now and then too. I'll be honest lad, life on your homeworld seems awful, and I've roughed it up myself all over my homeworld too. But you survived to make it here. Things are only gonna get a lot better.

I like the stuff for cooking. I've never had a problem with making stews or grilling the cuts of meat on the open but there's things like the kettle that would've been nice to have. Just being able to have electricity connected to a power grid heat up water is a lot easier to deal with than getting a campfire up. Tylian, you would be surprised that not that many villagers actually knew how to start campfires.

You'd think an entire society of peasant-survivors would know more on living out in the woods, huh? One time me and my buddies were attached to a battalion that had recently won their first battle. They were understandably high on their victory against the enemy but they all seemed to egg my boys on claiming that we were too old to fight this war... One of these guys... No coal for the grill, so he started shoving wet, thick firewood into it. Nearly burnt himself after trying to pour gasoline in and lighting up the grill.

[The convo appears to continue on for some time, with Bada continuing to tell his life story to Tylian]

''They were a pathetic lot, squandering their time to drink moonshine and fight over scraps. An offering of a jar of spirits garnered me their quick attention, but I sensed betrayal in their eyes. As I turned to walk away, one struck my armor with a rock. Were they mad?''
